---
title: "Burnout and Mental Health in Pediatric Dental Residency: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Residents and Directors"
author: "Loyola University Chicago Center for Data Science and Consulting"
format: pdf
editor: visual
---

# Summary

In this study, we analyzed data within residents and directors, then compared the groups' answer selections, informing the difference that various factors can have on a resident's wellbeing and experience in their program, and if the directors have a different perception of what residents face during residency. 
Out of 81 test within the residents group, we found 5 to be significant, but because of the amount of tests, zero were significant after adjusting for the false discovery rate. 
Out of 14 tests for directors, we found 0 to be true both before and after adjustment. 
We had a total of 119 residents and 24 directors in our data, which for some questions with many categorical responses, made it difficult to find significance. 
However, when cross-comparing the groups on each common question, we found 20/51 comparisons to be significant, 18 after adjustment. This means that at least 18 questions saw significant evidence of being answered differently for residents and directors. 
All significant tests will be reported in the results section, and their significance before and after adjustment will be noted.

# Methods

For our methodology, we conducted Fisher exact tests, which can calculate exact probabilities to see if there's a non-random association between groups. A low p-value (after adjustment) translates to having significant evidence for there existing some association between questions.

For questions that had multiple parts, we had to split them into individual questions (e.g. 13a, 13b, 13c...) to see if there were specific responses that were influenced by the grouping variable in question, which was the role (being a resident/director) in the case of cross-comparison, or information like program, experience, etc. In practice, this saw us, for example, analyzing whether directors perceive residence having negative impact on marriage versus whether residents feel their residency having a negative impact on marriage. The same question was asked for personal health care, control over one's life, and work/life balance. This example came from data from question 13 on the director's survey to illustrate the complexity of certain questions.

Then, to visualize the difference, we created side-by-side bar charts which plot the distribution of question responses versus the grouping variable. For resident/director comparison, this shows side-by-side plots of the residents' response to a question versus the directors'. Noticeable/interesting plots and findings were placed in the "significant findings" section of this writeup and all plots, significant or not, are in the appendix.

```{r validation-function, echo=FALSE}
# when trying to cross reference one question (question1) by another grouping variable (question2) 
validation <- function(question1, question2, data){
  df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      response1 = .data[[question1]],
      response2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
  
  comparison_res <- df %>%
    group_by(response1, response2) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(response2) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()

  table_comparison <- table(df$response2, df$response1)
#table_hours
  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table_comparison))
  
  if (mean(test$expected <= 5) < 0.8 | any(test$expected < 1)){
    fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
    if (fish_test$p.value <= 0.05){
     significant <- TRUE
   }
   else {
      significant <- FALSE
   }
    return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "fisher"))
  }
  else{
    if (test$p.value <= 0.05){
     significant <- TRUE
   }
   else {
      significant <- FALSE
   }
    }
  return(c("question1", "question2", round(test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "chisq"))
}
```

```{r residents-running, echo=FALSE}
  Question1 = character(),
  Question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(),
  Significant = logical(),

)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(question_dic_res))) {

  res_results[i, ] <- validation(
    question1 = question_dic_res$question1s[i],
    question2 = question_dic_res$question2s[i],
    data = f_res_coalesced
  )
}

res_results <- res_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    Question1 = question_dic_res$question1s, 
    Question2 = question_dic_res$question2s
  ) %>% arrange(Adj_P)
```

```{r barplot-function, echo=FALSE}
stack_bar <- function(q_reference, q_group, data){
  bar_df <- data %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_reference]], .data[[q_group]]) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_group]]) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = .data[[q_reference]], y = percent, fill = .data[[q_reference]])) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[q_group]])) +
    labs(
      title = paste(q_reference, "vs", q_group, sep = " "),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Percent of responses"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
  return(p)
}

```

# Significant Findings

## Residents Significance 

Questions 13d and 2, 13h and 2, 18 and 11, 16d and 3, 17 and 10 were all found to be significant before adjustment. 

The contexts of these questions and plots are as follows: 

13d/2: Treating patients as impersonal objects and PGY level 

13h/2: Not caring about what happens to certain patients and PGY level 

18/11: Working hours/week and desire to quit residency training 

16d/3: Experiencing sexual harassment and gender 

17/10: On call days/month and quality of life 

```{r}
plots_res_sig <- plots_res[c(22, 49, 73, 75, 79)]
walk(plots_res_sig, print)
```


## Directors Significant 

Little significance was found between directors, possibly due to low sample size, and none of the tests saw a p-value below 0.2. 

## Cross-Comparison Significance

Many questions were found to be significant between residents and directors, and below are all the questions that they responded significantly differently to: 

3: Gender 

12: Recreation hours per week

13a/b/c/f: Feeling emotionally drained, fatigued, strained at work, not caring about what happens to patients

14a/b: Negative impact on marriage, personal healthcare 

15a: Experienced discrimination based on gender

19: Frequency of meeting with director

20a/b/d: Frequency of discussing burnout, depression, quitting residency
  - notably, the only insignificant subquestion concerned suicidal thoughts
  
21: Presence of standardized criteria for screening burnout & mental health

22a/b/c: Satisfaction with how program manages burnout, depression, suicide

26: Setting for screening (Anonymously vs Confidentially)

```{r}
plots_res_sig <- plots_res[c(2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 17, 18, 21, 30, 31, 32, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 50)]
walk(plots_res_sig, print)
```
